test.title: Penn Admissions - Testing and English Proficiency

test_policy.notes: SAT or ACT required for all first-year applicants (domestic and international). Applicants facing hardship (e.g. no test center access) can submit a waiver. No minimum score; superscoring applied.

requirements.notes: Penn short-answer prompts (thank-you note, community, plus a school-specific prompt). One core-subject teacher recommendation plus the counselor recommendation; a second teacher/supporter letter is optional. CSS Profile applies to non-US-citizen aid applicants (plus tax or earnings statement). Interview policy not confirmed on pages checked.

deadlines.label: Early Decision (binding)
deadlines.notes: Decision released in December (exact date announced a week ahead).

deadlines.label: Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: Decision released in April (exact date announced a week ahead).

deadlines.label: Financial aid, Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: International students must apply for aid at the same time as for admission.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Exempt if English was your primary language of instruction for at least three years (high school, college, or both) by the time you enroll. Official scores only, from tests taken on or after 2025-04-01. Penn does not accept MyBest, IELTS Indicator or IELTS One Skill Retake.

english.notes: Competitive applicants tend to have 100 or higher (older 0-120 scale, taken within two years of the deadline). Not a hard minimum.
Competitive applicants tend to have a composite of 5 or above on the new 1-6 scale.
IELTS Academic; competitive applicants tend to have 7 or above.
Competitive applicants tend to have 130 or above.

aid.notes: Need-aware for international applicants (non-citizens/non-permanent residents of the US, Canada and Mexico); admitted aid recipients get need-based aid covering 100% of demonstrated need. Aid must be requested at the time of application and cannot be added later. No merit aid (awards are need-based).

majors.notes: Applicants apply to one of Penn's four undergraduate schools.

majors.program: School of Engineering and Applied Science

tier_notes.computer_science: Top-20 CS in Penn Engineering (strong in robotics and AI).
tier_notes.business: Wharton is the #1 US undergraduate business program.
tier_notes.biology_life_sci: Top-10 life sciences with Perelman School of Medicine on campus.
tier_notes.pre_med: Penn Medicine on campus gives top-5 research access and medical-school outcomes.
tier_notes.nursing: Penn Nursing is the #1 US undergraduate nursing program.
tier_notes.engineering: Penn Engineering is solid but ranked below its Wharton and arts & sciences peers.
tier_notes.arts_design: Weitzman School (architecture, fine arts) is mainly graduate; undergraduate arts are modest.
